subject: Phased Dedicated Commit proposal — term options, ramp and start date
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightscale.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightscale.ai, Nora Patel <nora@brightscale.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Revisiting Dedicated pricing & start timeline

Sean — thanks for the demo last week. BrightScale is ready to move from pilot to a production Dedicated pool, but we need a clear committed offer for procurement. A few specifics procurement asked for: 

- Product: Dedicated GPU pool (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) sized to sustain ~2.5k tokens/sec peak across 8 concurrent model endpoints.
- Term options: procurement wants pricing for 12 / 24 / 36‑month reserved commits and the associated discounts off on-demand.
- Ramp: we need a phased ramp plan — target capacity start 2026-07-01, with a 60/30/10 ramp across 3 months or an alternative phased schedule if that helps the pricing.
- SLA/throughput guarantee language and an estimate of when capacity would switch from pilot to reserved capacity (we aren't willing to pay for capacity before it's usable).

Attached is our RFP Q2 with usage profile and expected growth. Can you send a proposed term sheet and a recommended ramp schedule + any buyout/fallthrough language? Procurement also asked if you can start capacity earlier for an extra one-time fee.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Wu
VP Engineering, BrightScale AI
Attachment: BrightScale_RFP_Q2.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightscale.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-10 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revisiting Dedicated pricing & start timeline

Alex — appreciate the clear asks and the RFP. High level response below; I'll follow up with a short term sheet and a ramp calendar by EOD. Quick notes up front:

- Terms we typically quote: 12m / 24m / 36m reserved commits. Discount tiers increase with term length and with committed % of baseline (we can show both per-GPU and blended per-token economics).
- Start date: we can target 2026-07-01 as a soft start (provisioning & onboarding), with billing start tied to "capacity available for customer use" — we can define this as acceptance testing complete or X% capacity online. That avoids charging before usable.
- Ramp: 60/30/10 across months 1/2/3 is a standard phased ramp for us. We can also offer a 50/30/20 variant with a deeper up-front discount if BrightScale commits to earlier billing start.
- Early start premium: yes — we can prioritize capacity in the provisioning queue for a one-time expedite fee. I'll include two expedite levels (14-day and 30-day).

I'll attach a draft SOW + our standard Dedicated commit terms. Karthik will chime in on sizing/throughput SLAs.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Draft_SOW_v1.docx (docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revisiting Dedicated pricing & start timeline

Looping in pricing context for the team — Sean, when you share the term sheet include both:

- Unit economics: per-GPU/month list price, effective per-1k-token cost at the expected utilization bands (50/70/90%).
- Discount structure: fixed percentage by term (12/24/36) and an incremental growth credit if BrightScale increases committed baseline mid-term.
- Ramp protection: define a no-charge provisioning window and a clear acceptance test checklist so procurement is comfortable.

Also, propose a 24-month preferred pricing where we front-load a modest additional discount for the first 6 months in exchange for splitting the commitment in two equal tranches (billing starts on first tranche acceptance, second tranche on month 7) — this helps their cash flow and gives us predictable capacity planning.

Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <nora@brightscale.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-11 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revisiting Dedicated pricing & start timeline

Alex — quick technical confirmation from Karthik on sizing and guarantees:

- Sizing: to meet ~2.5k tokens/sec peak across 8 endpoints we recommend a baseline pool of 16 x H100-equivalent GPUs (assuming quantized 8-bit models and average sequence length 512). That provides room for KV cache utilization and headroom for spikes.
- Throughput SLA: we can commit to 99.5% availability at baseline throughput per endpoint and provide a throughput credit mechanism (token-based credit) if sustained throughput drops below agreed thresholds. SLA details will be in the Dedicated terms.
- Ramp plan options (pricing impact noted):
  * Standard phased: Month1 60% baseline (10 GPUs), Month2 90% (14 GPUs), Month3 100% (16 GPUs).
  * Accelerated start: Month1 80% (13 GPUs) then Month2 100% — triggers a 6% one-time surcharge for expedited capacity.

- Capacity start definition: "Capacity acceptance" = smoke tests pass + 80% of projected endpoints responding within latency SLOs for a 48-hour window. Billing start tied to acceptance.

I'll include sample throughput matrices by model family in the term sheet.

Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@brightscale.ai>, procurement@brightscale.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-12 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased Dedicated Commit proposal — term options, ramp and start date

Alex / team — attached is a concise term sheet and three pricing rows (12 / 24 / 36m) with the ramp schedules spelled out and an expedite fee table. Highlights: 

- 12-month: 18% off on-demand list, billing starts at capacity acceptance. Standard phased ramp (60/30/10).
- 24-month: 28% off on-demand list, option A (standard ramp) or Option B (split-tranche billing: first tranche immediate, second tranche billing month 7) — Option B includes extra 3% effective discount in months 1–6.
- 36-month: 35% off on-demand list, best blended economics, includes flexible mid-term growth credit (applies once per 12-month window).

- Expedited provisioning: 14-day expedite = one-time 6% surcharge on first-month invoice; 30-day expedite = 3% surcharge.
- Acceptance & billing: billing will not start until "capacity acceptance" as defined in the SOW. If BrightScale requests earlier pre-provisioning we will invoice the expedite fee and list the expected early-start date.

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Commit-Terms-2026.pdf (pdf) and Draft_SOW_v1.docx. Please review; if this looks aligned I'll convert the SOW to a DocuSign for signatures and share the HubSpot deal link.

Next steps: Alex — confirm preferred term (12/24/36), agree ramp option (standard vs split-tranche vs accelerated), and whether you want expedited provisioning. Procurement — if you need contract language changes send redlines to marissa_cole@redwood.com.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood-Dedicated-Commit-Terms-2026.pdf (pdf)
